recommendation.rationale: S3 states that, in the case of radiologically documented size progression of an isolated pulmonary nodule -- characterized by a volume-doubling time below 400 days -- definitive pathological clarification should be pursued, in a patient >=18 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised. VDT<400 is the guideline's own quantitative characterization of this progression criterion, not a second, independently required progression finding. The primary S3 guideline names three procedures for this confirmation -- bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy, CT-guided transthoracic biopsy, or minimally invasive surgical resection -- presented as coequal alternatives with no source-stated ranking or sequence between them; the source states the choice among them is made interdisciplinarily, involving pulmonology, radiology, and thoracic surgery, and this app does not select a procedure on its own. This branch does not use PET-CT, the Brock/Herder risk models, the >8mm initial-assessment pathway, any additional VDT threshold, or any minimum persistence duration -- none is stated by the source for this criterion. The app does not calculate VDT itself -- it is an explicit clinician entry. A same-source B1 discharge rule (ACR-S3-FOLLOWUP-DISCHARGE-VOLUME-OR-VDT) with unresolved status (s3_volume_stability_criterion_met absent) does not block this match, per the governed directional relation declared above (ADR-0011).
